title: Adiabatic compression of air is steeper than isothermal
caption: Compressing air (γ = 1.4) to 1/20 of its volume: along the isotherm pV = constant the pressure rises 20-fold (T stays 300 K); along the adiabat pV^γ = constant it rises 66.3-fold, because the gas also heats up. T₂ = 300 × 20^0.3999999999999999 = 994 K, which is 994 K from the pressure ratio 66.3/20. At any point the adiabat is 1.4 times as steep.
alt: p–V graph with pressure and volume as ratios to the start: the isotherm and the steeper adiabat both start at (1, 1); at V = 0.05 the isotherm is at 20 and the adiabat at 66.3.
description: Both axes are ratios to the starting state: V/V₁ (from 1 down to 1/20) and p/p₁.
Adiabat p = V^−1.4 reaches 20^1.4 = 66.3 there, and starts 1.4 times as steep: dp/dV = −γp/V against −p/V.
The temperature ratio is the pressure ratio ÷ 20: 3.31, so T₂ = 994 K.
